name: async-applyeach-curried-sc-broker
behavioral_change: In async v_new (3.0.0), `applyEach` and `applyEachSeries` became curried: instead of executing the functions immediately and calling the last argument as the completion callback, they always return a function that must be invoked with the completion callback. The function name and argument count are unchanged and no exception is raised; under the old calling form the completion callback is treated as an ordinary argument and the returned function is discarded, so no function runs and the callback never fires.
downstream_effect: In sc-broker, `_passThroughMiddleware` uses `applyEachSeries` to chain subscribe and publish middleware; after the upgrade the broker neither runs the middleware nor calls back, so every subscribe and publish stalls and the client-side tests fail with timeouts and `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: false == true`. The stack frames point only at test/main.js and the client index.js, while the code to edit is scbroker.js:235 in a separate broker process; neither scbroker.js nor `applyEach` appears in the output.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes one line in scbroker.js, replacing `async.applyEachSeries(self._middleware[type], req, function (err) {...})` with `async.applyEachSeries(self._middleware[type], req)(function (err) {...})`.
documented_in: The async 3.0.0 CHANGELOG (Breaking Changes) announces the simpler interface of `applyEach`/`applyEachSeries`, and the API reference at https://caolan.github.io/async/v3/docs.html#applyEach shows the new code form (`const appliedFn = async.applyEach(...)` followed by `appliedFn((err, results) => {`). The changelog entry itself contains no code; the code form comes from the API reference of the same version.
